root_idea.summary: A containing or enclosing surround: something that encircles another thing and holds it.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends from the eyelid and sword sheath to food vessels and to the grapevine conceived as a holder or support for grapes. Related classical usages name associated plant parts and other receptacles.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural جِفَان is presented under the supported singular dictionary citation form جَفْنَة.

senses.definition: A large bowl or serving vessel used for food.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural جِفَان, used for food vessels compared with large reservoirs or basins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter a she-camel and give her flesh as food to people in bowls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form I verbal usage describing slaughter together with feeding the people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or prepare bowls of food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported gloss is qualified as probably referring to preparing bowls of food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a grapevine, to attain the state of having a stock or root.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical usage; the identification of the relevant أصل as a stock is reported tentatively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The eyelid, whether upper or lower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The variant vocalization جِفْن is cross-referenced to this lexical item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper and lower surfaces of a bread-cake, taken together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning refers to the two surfaces collectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sheath or scabbard of a sword; reportedly also the larger case containing the sword and its fittings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The scabbard meaning is the commonly known one; the broader case meaning is explicitly reported as disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grapevine or its stock, climbing shoot or shoots, or leaves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports these as variant botanical applications rather than as a single fixed referent in every context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of grape, or the skin of a grape containing its juice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These fruit-related applications are reported as alternative classical identifications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The juice of the grapevine, or wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proposed explanation connects the expression with a progression through tears and rain before wine; that proposal is not treated as a separate ordinary meaning.
This is a conventional expression rather than the ordinary concrete meaning of جَفْن.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spreading plant whose dried form contracts and whose grains resemble fenugreek.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This lexical branch is listed without a more specific contextual description.
A figurative or analogical extension from the food bowl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A generous man who entertains and feeds many guests.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet for a renowned generous host, with the bowl serving as the basis of the metaphor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wine, or a kind of wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate lexical use of the noun from its food-vessel meaning.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Specialized she-camel slaughtering and feeding construction.
Making or preparing bowls of food.
Botanical usage concerning attainment of a vine stock.
Pointer-only entry directing the reader to Form II.
Upper and lower surfaces of a bread-cake.
Botanical, fruit, vine-juice, wine, and cloud-expression branches.
Food bowl or serving vessel, with plural information.
Small well by analogy with a food bowl.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural جِفَان; the public headword is normalized to the supported singular جَفْنَة.

Several grape-related meanings are reported as alternative classical applications, and the broader sword-case sense is explicitly disputed; they are retained with those qualifications rather than treated as universally interchangeable.
